<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />{{GHGmargin-letter|72|b}}
'''2.''' As in the case of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, the monosyllabic stem of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} generally takes the vowel which would have been required in the ''second'' syllable of the ordinary strong form, or which belonged to the ground-form, since this is essentially characteristic of the verbal form ({{GHGpar|43|b}}; {{GHGpar|67|b}}). However, it is to be remarked: (''a'') that the vowel, short in itself, becomes of necessity long in an open syllable as well as in a tone-bearing closed ''ultima'' (except in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, see d), e.g. 3rd ''sing. masc. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָם}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מָה}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מוּ}}, but in a closed ''penultima'' {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫מְתָּ}}, &c.<ref>In Aramaic, however, always {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מְתָּ}}; also in Hebrew grammars before Qimḥi {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מְתִּי}}, &c., are found, but in our editions of the Bible this occurs only in {{GHGterm|pause}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָ֑מְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫תְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=3.4}}.</ref>; (''b'') that in the forms as we now have them the lengthening of the original short vowel sometimes takes place irregularly. Cf. f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|c}}
Intransitive verbs ''middle e'' in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} have the form {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=he is dead}}; verbs ''middle o'' have the form {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר|translate=he shone}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּשׁ|translate=he was ashamed}}, {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב|translate=he was good}}.<ref>According to Stade ({{GHGcite|title=Grammatik}}, § 385 ''e'' and ''f'') the ''e'' in {{GHGheb|text=מֵת}} is of the nature of a diphthong (from ''ai'', which arose from the union of the vowel ''ĭ'', the sign of the intransitive, with the ''ă'' of the root), and likewise the ''o'' in {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר}}, &c. (from ''au''). But ''ô'' (from ''au'') could not, by {{GHGpar|26|p}}, remain in a closed penultima ({{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁתָּ}}, &c.); consequently the ''o'' of these forms can only be tone-long, i.e. due to lengthening of an original ''ŭ'', and similarly the ''ē'' of {{GHGheb|text=מֵת}} to lengthening of an original ''ĭ''. This is confirmed by the fact that the ''ō'' in {{GHGheb|text=בּשְׁתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁנוּ}} is always, and in {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שׁוּ}}, 3rd ''plur. perfect'', nearly always (the instances are 11 to 2), written defectively. Forms like {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫וֹשָׁה}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫וֹשׁוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרוּ}}, &c., are therefore due to orthographic licence.</ref> Cf. n–r.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|d}}
'''3.''' In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, and throughout {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} the short vowel of the preformatives in an open syllable before the tone is changed into the corresponding tone-long vowel. In {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} the original ''ă'' is the basis of the form and not the ''ĭ'' attenuated from ''ă'' ({{GHGpar|67|h}}; but cf. also h below, on {{GHGheb|text=יֵבוֹשׁ}}), hence {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, for ''yăqûm''; {{GHGheb|text=נָקוֹם}} for ''năqôm''; on the other hand, in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}} for ''hĭqîm''; {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵקִים}} (on the Ṣere cf. z); {{GHGterm|perfect Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּקַם}} for ''hŭqam''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|e}}
A vowel thus lengthened before the tone is naturally changeable and becomes {{GHGterm|vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} when the tone is moved forward, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְמִיתֶ֫נּוּ|translate=he will kill him}}; so also in the 3rd ''plur. imperfect Qal'' with ''Nûn paragogic''; {{GHGheb|text=יְמוּת֫וּן}} (without ''Nûn'' {{GHGheb|text=יָמ֫וּתוּ}}). The wholly abnormal ''scriptio plena'' of ''ē'' in {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֵימִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=11}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הֵמִיר}} in the same verse) should, with König, be emended to {{GHGheb|text=הֲיָמִיר}}; the incorrect repetition of the interrogative necessarily led to the pointing of the form as {{GHGterm|perfect}} instead of {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.—But in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} the ''û'' is retained throughout as an unchangeable vowel, when it has been introduced by an abnormal lengthening for the tone-long ''ō'' (as in the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}).
